claims.statement: The server exposes HTTP endpoints for monitoring: /healthz (liveness probe), /readyz (readiness probe), /metrics (Prometheus metrics), /config.json (non-sensitive configuration), and / (landing page).

Logs are structured and privacy-preserving by design, containing only timestamp, component name, slot UUID, error code (if applicable), and HTTP method/path/status code, while explicitly excluding IP addresses, user agents, file names/sizes, slot codes, and transfer contents.
When using Redis/Valkey for storage, keys automatically expire after the slot TTL period (default: 10 minutes), requiring no manual cleanup under normal operation.
No backup of Redis is required for the signaling server function as it only stores ephemeral slot state that is short-lived and recoverable by clients retrying with a new code.
When schedule mode is enabled via GMMFF_SCHEDULE_ENABLED=true, a background goroutine periodically cleans up expired schedule files according to the GMMFF_SCHEDULE_CLEANUP_INTERVAL cron expression.

For production deployments, a reverse proxy (such as NGINX, Caddy, or Traefik) should handle TLS termination, rate limiting, and request routing, with the gmmff server listening only on localhost or within a trusted network.

All configuration is done via environment variables with the GMMFF_ prefix, including GMMFF_ADDR (TCP address), GMMFF_SERVER (WebSocket URL), GMMFF_REDIS_URL (Redis connection), and logging/configuration options.
The application validates configuration on startup and will exit with an error message if the configuration is invalid.
